question: Absence of fetal heart sounds on auscultation with a Pinard stethoscope or Doppler is sufficient to confirm a diagnosis of stillbirth and inform the family.

l10n.wrongAnswerMessage: Correct. Stillbirth must NEVER be confirmed by auscultation alone. Real-time ultrasound confirming absence of cardiac activity is mandatory before informing the family — this is both a clinical and ethical requirement.
l10n.correctAnswerMessage: This is incorrect and potentially harmful. Auscultation alone is unreliable — fetal heart sounds can be missed due to maternal obesity, operator technique, or equipment limitations. Stillbirth must always be confirmed by real-time ultrasound before informing the family.
